thread:
arjun: Heads-up — after the strict fncall schema rollout this morning we're seeing a jump in rejects and some weird quota attribution across routes. Not just more rejects, but billing attribution seems to point to the wrong route ids. anyone else?

maria: saw the alert. spike started ~08:12 UTC for a handful of customers. rejects are mostly 'invalid_tool_response' and 'missing_required_field' from the validator. routing_id on logs is empty for ~40% of those requests.

sam: empty routing_id sounds like pipeline-side tag loss. did we change the routing metadata emitter in the proxy yesterday?

arjun: yes — small change to reduce header size. it was supposed to be noop for routing tags but could've removed the route header on fallback path.

devops-bot: Alert: fncall.validator.rejects rate 4.1x baseline for service=invoke-gateway - started 2026-03-21T08:11:50Z :pagerduty.incident/PD-9832

jess: Is this just telemetry? or are actual customer requests being billed to wrong projects? we need to know for billing ops.

sam: quick triage: the validator runs after routing resolution. if routing_id is lost before validator emits, sample backfill can't join by request_id -> route. That would make billing attribution fallback to default route which may be wrong.

maria: repro snippet from logs (sanitized):
```
[08:12:03] request: id=abc123 route_id=null customer=acme fncall_payload={...}
[08:12:03] validator: reject invalid_tool_response reason=missing_key 'result'
[08:12:03] billing: attribute request abc123 -> default-route
```

arjun: two problems: 1) loss of routing metadata on specific code path (likely the fallback adapter), 2) validator rejects are too noisy and trigger full-cost accounting. For canary we wanted soft-validate until rollout is stable.

sam: Agreed. proposal: revert header change on proxy, and in parallel flip validator back to 'soft' mode for the canary cohort. soft mode: emit telemetry + sample payloads but return permissive response to caller. Should reduce customer-visible failures and misbilling.

jess: For console: we should surface a dashboard that joins validator rejects + routing coverage and shows 'unattributed' rejects. Right now console dashboards assume route tagging is always present, so they undercount. I'll mock a panel: reject_count by route_id (include 'unattributed') + recent sample payload link.

sre-robot: Note: reverting header change will require a canary deploy 10% -> 50% -> 100%. This will temporarily increase relay churn. Recommend adding a temporary feature flag to gate header behavior per-route.

maria: Also need a telemetry backfill plan. If we can't backfill routing_id for older rejects, at least we can mark those events as 'route_unknown' and exclude them from billing reconciliation. Ops, can you confirm?

jess: I'll open a console UX ticket to add 'route_unknown' filter and a link to sampled payloads. + a small query example for support:
```sql
-- find most recent unattributed validator rejects
SELECT ts, request_id, error_code FROM fncall_validator WHERE route_id IS NULL ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;
```

arjun: timeline: rollback header change to canary within 1 hour, flip validator to soft for canary cohort immediately, add support filter + dashboard patch EOD. Who owns the rollback?

sam: I'll take rollback (sam). will create a small PR and coordinate canary with SRE.

maria: I'll handle validator config toggle and sampling hook.

jess: I'll make the UX ticket and draft dashboard panels, then sync with billing to ensure 'route_unknown' events are excluded from invoices for a ~24h window while we fix backfill.

sre-robot: Canary schedule request logged: deploy/sam/header-revert -> 10% @ 08:45 UTC, 50% @ 09:10 UTC, 100% @ 09:40 UTC. Monitoring alert thresholds: reject-rate drop OR stable route coverage > 99%.

arjun: thanks. quick note: add a lightweight log streamer that includes request_id + route_id in the validator's error payload for easier postmortem. even if route is null, include proxy path so we can triage which adapter wiped it. small change but huge signal.

sam: ack, will include proxy_path. pushing PR now.

maria: leaving a TODO to review quota meter interactions — if attribute fallback caused quota to consume a different pool we might need to credit customers. billing ops pinged.

jess: :thumbsup: keep updates here. if anyone hits a regression during canary, ping PD-9832 and @oncall.

arjun: closing the loop: will create a postmortem template entry for schema-rollouts that must include 'route-tag regression' as a risk item. we missed that in the checklist.

maria: noted. thanks all.
